display.purpose: Post heroes, page headings, profile display names at maximum scale. Used sparingly — one per screen at most.

headline.purpose: Card titles, cafe names in listing views, section headings within content.

title.purpose: Structural labels — modal headings, form section names, sidebar section titles.

body.purpose: Post captions, review text, comment body. Line-height 1.714 for readability.

label.purpose: Badges, metadata chips, timestamps, navigation labels. Never uppercase.

shadows.name: structural
shadows.purpose: Sidebar at rest and hovered state, sheet/drawer panels. Marks navigation chrome as above the content layer.

shadows.name: ambient-card
shadows.purpose: Card component ambient containment signal. Not elevation — just discrete surface boundary.

motion.name: ease-out-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state transitions: sidebar expand, sheet open, hover state changes.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Label fade-in/out on sidebar expand, opacity transitions for inline elements.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Sidebar width transition, card hover border-color shift.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Primary CTA. Forest Teal background, white text. Used for the single most important action on a surface.

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action. Bordered, no fill. Becomes primary-teal bordered on hover.

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Action buttons inside content — Like, Comment, Share, Bookmark. Transparent at rest, linen-muted on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; background: transparent; color: #1f2937; padding: 0; height: auto; border: none; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: color 150ms; outline: none; } .ds-btn-ghost-icon { width: 24px; height: 24px; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: #0f766e; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(15,118,110,0.3); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-ghost:disabled { opacity: 0.5; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Form text field. Pure cream background, bordered. Focus shifts border to primary teal.
components.css: .ds-input { display: flex; width: 100%; height: 48px; padding: 0 16px; background: #fffdf8; color: #1f2937; border: 1px solid #e1d7c8; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 14px; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; outline: none; transition: border-color 200ms; box-sizing: border-box; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #6b7280; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #0f766e; } .ds-input:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

narrative.overview:
CafeStory is built for people who already know what they like — they don't need to be seduced by the interface, they need the interface to get out of the way. Every design decision is deliberate the way a single-origin roast profile is deliberate: each choice is made with a specific outcome in mind, nothing is added for decoration, and the result is judged by the experience it produces, not how it looks in a screenshot.

The system is warm without being sentimental. The palette draws from roasted tones and cafe environments — aged paper, dark espresso, muted brick — but warmth is delivered through color relationships and typographic weight, never through decorative layering or visual noise.

This system explicitly rejects: the noisy-blue corporate social feed; the utilitarian directory feel; the mass-produced AI-default warm-cream + teal + eyebrow-labels SaaS scaffold; and the engagement-metric-everywhere energy of Instagram clones.
keyCharacteristics: Single sans-serif (Inter) across all surfaces — no display pairing, no decorative type
Restrained color: Bloom Teal for actions, Brick Chaff for emotion, Caramel Crack for ratings only
Tonal depth: layers are separated by surface color shifts (Green Bean → Parchment Skin → Silver Skin), not shadow stacks
Sidebar-first navigation that expands on focus — chrome shrinks to let content breathe
Dark mode is first-class, not an afterthought: Italian Roast backgrounds, not inverted pastels

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Each color role is used for one semantic purpose only. Bloom Teal = action. Brick Chaff = emotion/danger. Caramel Crack = rating. Never borrow a role color for a non-role purpose.

rules.name: The Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: Depth between layers is created by stepping through the neutral ramp (background → surface → surface-muted), never by stacking box-shadows on content cards.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Content surfaces — post cards, cafe cards, comment threads — have no elevation shadow at rest. If an element needs a shadow to feel distinct, check whether a tonal background shift would serve better first.

rules.name: The No-Display-In-UI Rule
rules.body: Body copy, button labels, form fields, and navigation items always use Body or Label scale. Display and Headline are for content identity, not chrome.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is communicated first through font-weight, then through size. Use weight contrast (400 → 700 → 900) to do the heavy lifting.

dos: Do keep Bloom Teal (#0f766e) exclusive to interactive actions and current selection.
Do separate content layers through background tonal shifts (Green Bean → Parchment Skin → Silver Skin) before reaching for a shadow.
Do use font-weight contrast (400 → 700 → 900) as the primary hierarchy tool within a given type size.
Do maintain ≥4.5:1 contrast for all body and placeholder text against their background — verify at the border cases (Ash Gray on Parchment Skin, Ash Gray on Silver Skin).
Do support @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) for all transitions.
Do use Inter system-stack fallback so the layout doesn't shift if the web font is slow.
Do keep the sidebar nav labels hidden at rest and revealed on hover/focus only.
Do use the dark mode token mapping consistently — map each role token to its dark counterpart explicitly.
donts: Don't make the interface feel like Facebook/generic social feed — too noisy, too blue, too many competing elements on screen at once.
Don't use the Yelp/TripAdvisor utilitarian directory pattern.
Don't use the generic SaaS warm-cream body + teal primary + uppercase eyebrow label scaffold.
Don't clone the engagement-metric-everywhere energy of Instagram — social counters are present but subordinate.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards or list items.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient). Use solid color.
Don't use Caramel Crack (#d97706) for anything other than rating scores.
Don't use decorative motion — page-load choreography or scroll-triggered entrance stacks applied uniformly.
Don't use a display or headline font weight in navigation labels, button text, or form fields.
